parameters.content:
## Betterstack → Zendesk Receiver

**Purpose**: Real-time webhook receiver for Betterstack incident events.
Mirrors incident lifecycle into Zendesk tickets via tag-based state.

**Webhook URL**: `https://twofifteen.app.n8n.cloud/webhook/betterstack-incident`

**Auth**: Built-in Webhook node `headerAuth`, backed by `httpHeaderAuth`
credential `Betterstack Webhook Auth` (header `X-Webhook-Auth`, value
`Bearer <token>`). Mismatch returns HTTP 403 from the Webhook node itself,
before the workflow fires. n8n Cloud does not expose `$env`, so the
credential pattern is the only viable option here.

**Companion workflows**:
- Resolve sub-workflow `FXjwcoWpPhmv76ws` (called for resolutions)
- Polling reconciler (5-min fallback for missed resolution webhooks)

**Spec**: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-09-betterstack-zendesk-incident-workflow-design.md`

## Event-type Discriminator

Betterstack docs only document the top-level `event` field for `comment`
events. For started / acknowledged / resolved / reopened, we MUST inspect
`data.attributes` timestamps:

| Condition | Branch |
|---|---|
| `resolved_at != null` | resolved (output 0) |
| `acknowledged_at != null && resolved_at == null` | acknowledged (output 1) |
| both null | started (output 2) |

**Switch fallback**: `fallbackOutput: "none"` — if a payload matches no
branch (shouldn't happen given the discriminator covers all 3 states),
the Switch silently drops it rather than crashing.

## v1 Trade-off: Ack-Before-Create

If an `acknowledged` webhook arrives before `started` (out-of-order delivery),
the ack lookup finds no ticket and the branch no-ops — the ack comment is
lost. The subsequent `started` webhook will still create the ticket and the
`resolved` webhook will still resolve it; only the ack-comment annotation is
missing.

We accept this in v1 rather than queueing pending acks. If this becomes a
real operational issue, switch to a Code-node-buffered approach in v2.

Ack idempotency sentinel = `betterstack-acked` tag. Set in the same Zendesk
update call as the ack comment so a failed comment write never poisons the
sentinel.

## Edge Case: Resolved Without Create

If the `resolved` webhook arrives but no open ticket exists (the `started`
webhook was dropped), the FALSE branch creates the ticket directly in
`solved` state with the resolution comment baked in.

**Duplication note**: The resolution-comment formatter is duplicated
between `Format Resolution Comment (Pre-create)` here and `Compute Downtime
+ Format Comment` in the resolve sub-workflow. Both must stay in lockstep.
A shared "format comment" sub-workflow would centralize this, but adds an
extra hop for one extra caller — accepted as the cleanest n8n-native option.

## Started Branch: Reopen vs Create

1. **Editable ticket exists** (`status<closed`) → reopen: status=open,
   swap `betterstack-resolved` → `betterstack-open`, append "reopened" comment.
2. **No editable ticket but a closed ticket exists** → create a NEW ticket
   tagged `reopened`, with a comment linking back to the closed original.
   (Zendesk auto-closes solved tickets after 24h and `closed` is terminal.)
3. **No ticket at all** → fresh create (the normal new-incident path).

All tag mutations happen in a single Zendesk update call per branch.

## Create-node Body Construction

**Description vs Comment**: Zendesk's ticket-create API auto-creates the
first ticket comment from the `description` parameter when no explicit
`comment` is provided. Passing BOTH `description` and `comment` produces
a duplicate first comment.

Rule applied here:
- **Fresh + Linked + Solved creates** → set `description` only. No `comment`
  inside `additionalFieldsJson`.
- **Updates** (ack, reopen, resolve) → set `comment` with `public: false`.
  Updates do not have a `description` parameter.

**Newline handling**: The fresh-ticket / linked-ticket descriptions are
built via raw string concatenation in expressions — `"\n"` literals end
up as actual newline characters in the final string. Zendesk's
`description` parameter accepts literal newlines, so no JSON wrapping is
needed. The solved-ticket path uses `description: $json.comment` where
`$json.comment` already contains literal newlines from the Code node.

**If we ever switch to passing description inside `additionalFieldsJson`**
(i.e. as a JSON-encoded body), the description text MUST be wrapped in
`JSON.stringify` to escape special chars. Today's structure avoids this
because `description` is a top-level node parameter, not part of the JSON
body.

## Routing & Assignment Config (constants)

Set at the top of `receiver.workflow.ts`:

- `GROUP_ID = 360021265172` — Zendesk group "System Administration"
- `ASSIGNEE_USER_ID = 387328728671` — Zendesk user "Robby Barnes" (robby@215.tech)
- `REQUESTER_USER_ID = 26045726036621` — Zendesk user "Better Stack" (betterstack@215.tech)
- `CATEGORY_FIELD_ID = 360048770292` / `CATEGORY_VALUE = "network"` — Zendesk Category custom field set on EVERY ticket create (fresh, linked, solved-edge-case)
- `TICKET_TYPE = "incident"` — Zendesk SYSTEM `type` field. Set on every ticket create AND required when transitioning to solved.
- `PRIORITY = "high"` — per spec default
- `COMMENT_PUBLIC = true` — matches Zapier zap
- `RESOLVE_SUBWORKFLOW_ID` — `FXjwcoWpPhmv76ws` (Phase 1)

Auth credential `Betterstack Webhook Auth` (`httpHeaderAuth`) must exist
in n8n with the bearer token wired into Betterstack's outgoing webhook.
